original_value: The task of Visual Question Answering (VQA) has emerged in recent years for its potential applications. To address the VQA task, the model should fuse feature elements from both images and questions efficiently. Existing models fuse image feature element vi and question feature element qi directly, such as an element product viqi. Those solutions largely ignore the following two key points: 1) Whether vi and qi are in the same space. 2) How to reduce the observation noises in vi and qi. We argue that two differences between those two feature elements themselves, like (vi − vj) and (qi −qj), are more probably in the same space. And the difference operation would be beneficial to reduce observation noise. To achieve this, we first propose Differential Networks (DN), a novel plug-and-play module which enables differences between pair-wise feature elements. With the tool of DN, we then propose DN based Fusion (DF), a novel model for VQA task. We achieve state-of-the-art results on four publicly available datasets. Ablation studies also show the effectiveness of difference operations in DF model.

result.paraphrase: Visual Question Answering (VQA) has recently attracted attention because of its potential applications. Solving the VQA task requires efficiently fusing feature elements from both images and questions. Existing approaches combine image feature element vi and question feature element qi directly, for example through element-wise products viqi. However, these methods largely overlook two important issues: 1) whether vi and qi lie in the same space, and 2) how to reduce observation noise in vi and qi. We contend that differences between the two feature elements themselves, such as (vi − vj) and (qi − qj), are more likely to be in the same space, and that the difference operation can help reduce observation noise. To this end, we first introduce Differential Networks (DN), a novel plug-and-play module that enables differences between pair-wise feature elements. Using DN, we further propose DN based Fusion (DF), a new model for the VQA task. It achieves state-of-the-art results on four publicly available datasets, and ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of difference operations in the DF model.
